items.text: Every neurotic is a living repetition machine: fantasies enshrined in the unconscious personality are repeated over and over again.

Neurosis is, as Freud proved fifty years ago, an anachronism: it is the perpetuation of unconscious wishes and defense mechanisms stemming from early childhood, which every human being harbors or produces in transitory phases in the first five years of life.
A simple yardstick for recognizing neurosis is the lack of ability to work, to love (tenderly and with normal potency retained), to have normal social contacts and interests, to enjoy one's hobbies.
One has to take into account the fact that every neurosis involves deep unconscious pleasures and self-damaging tendencies.

Expressed differently, Freudian psychoanalysis has proven in fifty years of clinical experience that certain unconscious behavior pat- terns acquired in early childhood become petrified, and under the pressure of the "unconscious repetition compulsion" (Freud) are re- peated throughout the remainder of life with eternal monotony- and completely without conscious awareness of that repetition.
